name: MonarchAiOnboardingTour
title: AiOnboardingTour
wrapsNative: TabView with .tabViewStyle(.page(indexDisplayMode: .never)) for the steps, MonarchStepper for the position, MonarchButton for Back, Next and Turn off AI; presented by the app in sheet(isPresented:content:) with presentationDetents
summary: A short, step-by-step introduction to AI in a product (what it can see, what it can do, how to turn it off) with Back, Next and Turn off AI on every step.
whenToUse: The first time people meet AI features in a product, in a sheet or at the top of a screen, to explain what the assistant sees and does and how to switch it off.
whenNotToUse: To point at one control use TipKit's popoverTip(_:arrowEdge:). For a general setup checklist use MonarchOnboardingChecklist.
api: MonarchAiOnboardingTour.init(_ steps: [MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep], labels: MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels = MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(), onSkip: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDisable: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, onFinish: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)

MonarchAiOnboardingTour.init(_ steps: [MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep], step: Binding<Int>, labels: MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels = MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(), onSkip: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDisable: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, onFinish: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)
MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep.init(_ title: String, id: String? = nil, body: String, systemImage: String? = nil)

appearance: The AI strong colour on the glyph and the "AI" eyebrow, headings in default text and bodies in muted text, the stepper's colours, a primary Next button, a secondary Back button and a ghost Turn off AI button. No surface of its own: the sheet or a MonarchCard provides it. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web's target option, which outlines an element on the page, has no equivalent: use TipKit's popoverTip to point at a control. The web's floating placement becomes a sheet presented by the app. Steps are swiped as pages as well as moved with Back and Next. On the macOS host build, which is not a supported product, the current step is shown without paging. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: Each step's heading has the header trait, and VoiceOver focus moves to it when the step changes.
The stepper reads the position and the name of the step.
The close button is named "Skip introduction".
Turn off AI is on every step, so the opt-out is always reachable.
Every button has a 44-point touch target; the buttons stack when they do not fit on one line.
edgeCases: The tour takes the height of its tallest step, so pages do not jump in height and long text at large sizes is not clipped.
A step outside the range is clamped to the first or the last step.
Step ids default to the title; the stepper gets unique ids even when titles repeat.
